newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S.Australia gets OK for bulk handling sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S.Australia gets OK for bulk handling sale.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has cleared the way for the South Australian government to sell the bulk handling facilities around the State, State Treasurer Stephen Baker said on Monday.
The state government announced earlier this year it would enter into negotiations with the South Australian Co-operative Bulk Handling Ltd (SACBH) for the purchase of the facilities.
Baker said in a statement the government would introduce legislation next month covering third-party access and regulatory issues related to the sale.

The ACCC had indicated such an approach, providing legislative safeguards to ensure a reasonable access and competition framework, together with an effective dispute resolution procedure, was acceptable, Baker said.
"The ACCC has advised that it does not intend to oppose plans by the South Australian Government to sell its bulk handling facilities to SACBH," he said.
"However negotiations with SACBH will require that satisfactory agreement also be reached on other issues such as price," he said.

The facilities, for the transfer of bulk cargoes from stockpile to ship, are at Port Adelaide, Port Giles, Wallaroo, Port Pirie, Port Lincoln and Thevenard, and are currently owned and operated by the South Australian Ports Corporation.
Baker said it was logical for the government to offer SACBH first right of purchase because the future of the facilities was inextricably linked to the SACBG grain terminals.
